items.summary: The download re-download entitlement was stated as format-bound in four places in 20.06.03 (Role Lens, governing promise, Playback & Download Depth, D-01), contradicting the owning file 20.04.03, whose DT-05 explicitly rejected format-bound re-download and whose D-08 ratified a format-agnostic entitlement. Fixed the library file to state the canonical rule and cite it.
items.canonicalSource: 20.04-direct-to-fan-storefront/20.04.03-digital-sales-name-your-price-bundles.md:161 — "| D-08 | Download entitlement is format-agnostic and never expires | See DT-05. Buy the record, not a file; re-download any offered format forever. Reinforces the 'you own this' promise at zero storage cost. |"; :130 DT-05 — "❌ REJECTED — the fan buys **the record**, not a file. Binding the entitlement to a single format re-download is a streaming-era mistake: it means a fan who bought MP3 in 2026 and wants FLAC in 2029 has to re-buy."; :69-70 — "the entitlement is format-agnostic (one purchase entitles all offered formats — you bought the record, not a file), and re-downloading in a different format later is free and unlimited"; :95 (Edge Cases, User Sees column) — "Library, indefinitely, all offered formats"; :140 (Cross-Cut Notes) — "Delivers to 20.06.03 Fan Library & Collection — the entitlement's permanent, format-agnostic home"
items.classificationRationale: Both files carry numbered decisions, which normally signals OWNER — but they are not equally authoritative on this concept. 20.04.03 is the digital-sales file that creates the entitlement; it names 20.06.03 as merely 'the entitlement's permanent, format-agnostic home' (:140) and routes entitlement semantics to CX-M24 (:72). It adjudicated this exact question in a Deep Think row (DT-05), naming the alternative, naming the bought-MP3-want-FLAC scenario, and rejecting it as 'a streaming-era mistake' — then ratified the result as D-08. 20.06.03 never deliberated format scope at all: the string 'format-agnostic' appeared nowhere in it, no DT row considers the question, and its D-01 is substantively about persistence ('indefinitely', 'no expiry or count cap') with the format clause riding along as an unexamined restatement. That is drift from a settled decision, not a second decision. The owning file also already specifies what the library must show ('Library, indefinitely, all offered formats', :95), so the corrected text is fully determined by the canonical source — no product value was invented.
items.fixApplied:
Four edits to 20.06.03-fan-library-collection.md, all citing 20.04.03 D-08 (and DT-05 where the rejection matters):

1. Line 24 (Role Lens, Fan row) — "re-downloads in the format purchased" → "re-downloads in **any format the release offers** — not only the one they first took, because the entitlement is format-agnostic ([20.04.03](...) D-08)". Row still has 3 columns.

2. Lines 34-36 (governing promise) — "Re-downloadable indefinitely, in the formats purchased," → "Re-downloadable indefinitely, in **any format the release offers** — you bought the record, not a file ([20.04.03](...) D-08) —".

3. Lines 68-75 (Playback & Download Depth, Download bullet) — replaced "the fan re-downloads the **original purchased formats** (e.g. FLAC, WAV, MP3-320, ALAC — whatever the release offered and they bought)" with a format-agnostic bullet that: states re-download is in any format the release offers; cites D-08/DT-05 and reproduces the MP3-320-in-2026/FLAC-in-2029 case as normal behaviour; specifies the concrete UI consequence the collision turned on — a **format selector on every owned release** listing that release's offered formats (MP3-320, FLAC, WAV per 20.04.03) rather than a fixed purchased-format label; bounds it (a format the release never offered is not downloadable, because it does not exist); and adds 'no format-switch charge' alongside the existing no-expiry/no-count-cap clauses.

4. Line 174 (D-01) — "in the purchased formats" → "in **any format the release offers**", with a Context addition recording that format scope is not this file's to set, that 20.04.03 DT-05 rejected format-bound re-download outright, and that the library therefore renders a format selector. Row still has 3 columns.

The format enumeration was normalised to the canonical set in 20.04.03:67 (MP3 320 kbps, FLAC, WAV); the stray 'ALAC' example, which the owning file never offers, was dropped rather than carried forward.

items.downstreamNote: 20.06.03 now obliges a per-release format selector in the library UI, and CX-M24/CX-M10 must expose the release's offered-format set (not the purchase's format) on an owned item. This is the consequence the owning decision already implied — 20.04.03:95 promises the fan 'Library, indefinitely, all offered formats' — and is now stated on the surface that has to build it.
